chunks.content: 96 How to Buy a Business with $0 Down (No, Really) Hi Sara, Want to buy a business without spending a dime of your own money? It sounds like a scam, right? Like some late-night infomercial: “This one weird trick will make you a millionaire!” I promise you—it’s not. But before we get ahead of ourselves, let’s start with what doesn’t work: ❌ Convincing a seller to finance 100% of the deal (good luck with that). ❌ Finding a “free” business (if you’ve found one, it’s probably a terrible deal). ❌ Manifesting a business into existence (if only it were that easy). What does work is using an SBA 7(a) loan strategically. This program is already a game-changer in business acquisitions, offering financing up to 90%. But what if I told you that, in some cases, you can finance 100% of a deal—without putting in a single dollar of your own cash? Here’s the play: ➝ The SBA requires buyers to put down 10%, right? Well, some lenders will accept a seller note—a loan from the seller themselves—as that 10%. ➝ If structured correctly (meaning the note follows SBA rules, like a 24-month standby period), the bank treats it like a cash down payment. ➝ Result? You just bought a business with no money out of pocket. But Here’s the Catch... ➝ Not all banks do this. You need a preferred SBA lender who actually understands these deals. ➝ Your Letter of Intent (LOI) matters. If you try to sneak this in last minute, the seller will be less than thrilled. Transparency is key. ➝ “$0 down” doesn’t mean “free.” You still need funds for closing costs, loan origination fees, legal fees, and diligence expenses. The Takeaway? There’s an absolute wave of business owners looking to retire—millions of them, in fact. The opportunity is massive. But the people who win? They’re the ones who get creative with financing, work with the right banks, and structure deals that actually close. To buying businesses the smart way, Sara Sharp Partner, SK&S Law Group Business Consultant & Founder of Deal Academy P.S.
